summary: Small concurrent streaming connections from mobile SDK cause slot churn and transient GPU starvation in customer's Dedicated pool
description: Customer reports repeated p99 latency spikes and sustained throughput degradation in their Dedicated GPU pool starting 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC. Symptoms coincide with a morning traffic pattern where thousands of short streaming requests (100-500ms each) from the AtlasLearn mobile SDK fan out rapidly. The Dedicated autoscaler does not appear to add capacity in time; GPUs show frequent small allocation/eviction cycles and kernel queue stalls. This ticket captures the investigation into allocation churn, autoscaler responsiveness, and whether scheduling heuristics are unfairly favoring large-batch jobs, enabling slot fragmentation and transient starvation for small streams.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use AtlasLearn mobile client simulation script to open 4k concurrent streaming sessions over 2 minutes: python tools/sim_client.py --concurrency 4000 --stream-duration 0.2 --payload-size 1kb
2) Target the customer's Dedicated pool route: POST /v1/generate?pool=atlaslearn-dedicated with streaming SSE
3) Observe per-GPU allocation events via internal allocator endpoint: GET /internal/allocations?pool=atlaslearn-dedicated
4) Correlate with GPU queue depth and kernel errors from /metrics and NVidia dmon logs
observed_behavior:
- p99 generation latency from 400ms baseline to 2.8s during peak fanout.
- Autoscaler adds 0 or 1 GPUs (insufficient) while allocator shows dozens of short-lived slot allocations and evictions.
- GPU metrics show high context switch rate, small batch utilization (low GPU occupancy), and repeated 'allocation_timeout' traces.
- Some requests receive 429/503 when allocator can't satisfy short-lived slot requests.
expected_behavior:
- Autoscaler should provision additional GPUs to maintain latency SLOs for customer Dedicated pool during predictable fanout spikes, or the runtime should coalesce short streams to avoid allocation churn.
- No sustained kernel queue stalls or high eviction rate for small streaming jobs.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: high fanout of tiny streams causes allocator to create many ephemeral GPU slots, increasing scheduler overhead and preventing effective batching.
Metric evidence: per-GPU small-batch ratio jumped from 8% to 62% during spike (grafana: grafana.redwood/internal/d/alloc?panel=small_batch_ratio).
Observed allocator churn: average slot lifetime dropped to 210ms; eviction rate spiked to 38% (trace logs).
Autoscaler behavior: scaling loop has 30s evaluation window and requires >70% sustained utilization to scale — too coarse for sub-minute spikes. See scheduler autoscale SLOs in runbook.
No NVidia ECC errors or hardware faults found; noisy tenant behavior confirmed by tenant-level allocation heatmap.
Potential scheduling bug: recently landed change to 'short_stream_preemption' (runtime PR #4418) may prefer evicting older small-stream slots to free memory for larger batches, causing thrash under many small streams.
comments:
2026-03-10 06:10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Contacted customer for exact SDK version and their mobile traffic pattern. Customer confirmed they rolled a client update 2026-03-09 that enabled aggressive background prefetching.
2026-03-10 09:04 - Elena Morrison (SRE): Correlated allocator churn in us-west with customer's tenant id. Added temporary rate cap on slot-creates for tenant atlaslearn (applied policy: max_inflight_streams=1000) to reduce immediate thrash.
2026-03-11 02:30 - Thomas Nguyen (Runtime Eng): Investigated PR #4418; reproduced eviction pattern in staging with simulation. Proposed short-term revert and longer-term coalescing of small streams into multiplexed sessions.
2026-03-12 11:15 - Elena Morrison (SRE): After emergency rate cap and a small autoscaler config tweak (reduce scale threshold to 55% for dedicated pools during business hours), observed p99 fall back to 640ms. Customer report: significant improvement during morning peak.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: temporary tenant-level throttle on slot creation plus autoscaler sensitivity adjustment. Root cause appears to be a combination of (1) client-side behavioral change producing many short streaming requests and (2) runtime policy that aggressively evicts small-stream slots under memory pressure, which, under high fanout, produces allocation churn and starvation. A runtime code change (revert PR #4418) has been drafted and is planned for quick rollout to staging for validation.
workaround:
- Customer can enable SDK batching (client-side) to group small prompts into fewer long-lived streams.
- We've applied a tenant rate cap (max_inflight_streams=1000) and lowered autoscale threshold for the Dedicated pool as an immediate mitigation.
follow_up_actions:
Deploy revert of short_stream_preemption (runtime PR #4446) to staging and run AtlasLearn simulation suite.
Implement multiplexing/coalescing feature to allow many tiny streams to reuse existing slots (spec PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/specs/pull/89).
Add an autoscaler mode for rapid transient fanout events: evaluate 10s windows and allow temporary burst capacity.
Add customer-facing guidance in AtlasLearn onboarding to prefer SDK batching or multiplexed streams for mobile use-cases.
Postmortem to be authored and linked to this ticket within 7 days.
